Autocorrelation function

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. R returns numeric correlations; request plotting separately.

arima

MA(1) with intercept

Stata 

arima y, arima(0,0,1) vce(oim)

R stats 

stats::arima(y, order = c(0, 0, 1), method = "ML")

Differs from Stata Gaussian ML with observed-information covariance. Stata vce(oim) matches the R Hessian convention. For differenced models, the explicit time regressor supplies Stata drift; the seasonal drift regressor is time/4. Require a complete regularly spaced series.

rolling

Expanding-window recursive regression

Stata 

rolling _b, window(40) recursive: regress y x

R stats 

t(vapply(40:nrow(data), function(i) stats::coef(stats::lm(y ~ x, data[seq_len(i), ])), numeric(2)))

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Uses a fixed first observation and increasing estimation endpoint.

Stata reference · R reference

Rolling-window regression coefficients

Stata 

rolling _b, window(40): regress y x

R zoo 

zoo::rollapply(data, width = 40, FUN = function(z) stats::coef(stats::lm(y ~ x, data = as.data.frame(z))), by.column = FALSE, align = "right")

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Output rows correspond to complete right-aligned windows; failures need explicit handling in production.

tsfilter

Baxter-King approximate band-pass cycle

Stata 

tsfilter bk cycle = y, minperiod(6) maxperiod(32) smaorder(12)

R stats 

{ K <- 12; j <- -K:K; low <- 2 * pi / 32; high <- 2 * pi / 6; w <- ifelse(j == 0, (high - low) / pi, (sin(high * j) - sin(low * j)) / (pi * j)); w <- w - mean(w); stats::filter(y, w, sides = 2) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Symmetric finite-order band-pass filter loses endpoint observations.

Stata reference · R reference

Hodrick-Prescott trend and cycle decomposition

Stata 

tsfilter hp cycle = y, smooth(1600) trend(trend)

R base 

{ n <- length(y); D <- diff(diag(n), differences = 2); trend <- drop(solve(diag(n) + 1600 * crossprod(D), as.numeric(y))); data.frame(trend = trend, cycle = as.numeric(y) - trend) }

Differs from Stata Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Complete regular series; this direct penalized least-squares solution uses the two-sided HP filter.

Stata reference · R reference

Locate missing time periods

Stata 

tsreport, report

R base 

data.frame(previous = head(data$t, -1), next_time = tail(data$t, -1), gap = diff(data$t))[diff(data$t) != 1, ]

Fixed workflow; adapt the named data columns explicitly. Assumes integer unit-spaced time; date calendars need the intended interval definition.

Stata reference · R reference

tssmooth

Centered five-term moving average

Stata 

tssmooth ma smooth = y, window(2 1 2)

R zoo 

{ data$smooth <- as.numeric(zoo::rollapply(data$y, width = 5, FUN = function(v) if (all(is.na(v))) NA_real_ else mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), partial = TRUE, align = "center")); data }

Rows must be in time order with one row per equally spaced period. Partial endpoint windows and nonmissing observations receive equal normalized weights, matching Stata; an entirely missing window returns NA.

Rows must be in time order with one row per equally spaced period. Partial endpoint windows and nonmissing observations receive equal normalized weights, matching Stata; an entirely missing window returns NA.

var

Unrestricted bivariate VAR(1) by equation OLS

Stata 

var y x, lags(1) dfk small

R stats 

{ lagged <- transform(data, Ly = c(NA_real_, head(y, -1L)), Lx = c(NA_real_, head(x, -1L))); lagged <- lagged[-1L, ]; stats::lm(cbind(y, x) ~ Ly + Lx, data = lagged) }

Differs from Stata Unrestricted one-lag VAR on a complete ordered series. Stata dfk small matches OLS residual-df scaling and t/F tests. R explicitly creates both lagged regressors and uses a common estimation sample; trend is supplied on the original time scale.

Stata reference · R reference

VAR with deterministic time trend

R stats 

{ lagged <- transform(data, Ly = c(NA_real_, head(y, -1L)), Lx = c(NA_real_, head(x, -1L))); lagged <- lagged[-1L, ]; stats::lm(cbind(y, x) ~ Ly + Lx + trend, data = lagged) }

Differs from Stata Unrestricted one-lag VAR on a complete ordered series. Stata dfk small matches OLS residual-df scaling and t/F tests. R explicitly creates both lagged regressors and uses a common estimation sample; trend is supplied on the original time scale.

vec

Rank-one vector error-correction model

Match cointegrating-vector normalization before comparing coefficients.

Stata reference · R reference

wntestq

Ljung-Box test after AR(1) estimation

Stata 

predict e, residuals
wntestq e, lags(8)

R stats 

stats::Box.test(stats::residuals(fit), lag = 8, type = "Ljung-Box", fitdf = 0)

Differs from Stata After the same AR(1) fit, test its residuals with chi-square(8). fitdf=0 matches Stata wntestq; fitdf=1 would be a different residual-diagnostic convention.

Stata reference · R reference

Ljung-Box serial-correlation portmanteau test

Stata 

wntestq y, lags(8)

R stats 

stats::Box.test(y, lag = 8, type = "Ljung-Box")

Differs from Stata Ljung-Box Q uses eight autocorrelations and chi-square(8), matching wntestq. A complete regularly spaced series is required. Stata wntestq does not deduct fitted-model parameters.
